description: A focused information pack for ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), ATM-related disease, neurological and immune features, research and life with a rare inherited condition. It is an information-discovery aid, not medical advice.

synopsis.overview: Ataxia-telangiectasia (A-T), also called Louis-Bar syndrome, is a rare inherited disorder caused by variants in both copies of the ATM gene. It affects coordination and other nervous-system functions, immune defenses and the way cells respond to DNA damage.
synopsis.manifestations: Features often begin in early childhood and may include progressive balance and coordination problems, slurred speech, abnormal eye movements, small visible blood vessels on the eyes or skin, recurrent infections and delayed development. Cancer risk, lung disease, diabetes and other effects vary between people.
synopsis.management: Care is individualized and may involve neurology, immunology, respiratory, rehabilitation, speech and language, nutrition and cancer specialists. Supportive treatment can address infections, breathing, movement, communication and nutrition; clinicians also take radiation sensitivity into account when planning investigations or treatment.
synopsis.outlook: A-T is variable and currently has no cure. The course depends on the ATM variants and complications affecting each person; research and supportive care continue to develop. Prognosis should be discussed with the person’s specialist team rather than inferred from general information.

topics.heading: Clinical trials
topics.description: Registered A-T studies, including research into ATM-related biology, immune function, infections, cancer risk, rehabilitation and supportive interventions. A listing does not indicate eligibility or that a study is recommended.

termDefinitions.ataxia-telangiectasia clinical trial: A planned study involving people with A-T that evaluates an intervention or approach under a defined protocol.
termDefinitions.A-T clinical study: A structured investigation involving people with ataxia-telangiectasia; A-T is the common abbreviation for the condition.
termDefinitions.ATM clinical trial: A study involving ATM-related disease, biology or interventions.
termDefinitions.trial recruitment: The process of identifying and enrolling people who may take part in a clinical study.
termDefinitions.investigational: Being studied and not yet established or approved for the use being investigated.
termDefinitions.trial results: Findings reported after researchers analyse information collected during a clinical trial.

topics.heading: Treatment and supportive care
topics.description: Supportive care for movement, communication, immunity, infections, breathing, nutrition, development and other effects of A-T.

termDefinitions.immunoglobulin replacement: Infused or injected antibody treatment used for selected people whose immune systems do not make enough effective antibodies.
termDefinitions.infection prevention: Measures intended to reduce infection risk and identify or treat infections promptly.
termDefinitions.physical therapy: Rehabilitation focused on movement, strength, balance, function and safety.
termDefinitions.speech therapy: Assessment and therapy for communication, speech, swallowing or related needs.
termDefinitions.respiratory care: Assessment and support for breathing, airway clearance and recurrent lung problems.
termDefinitions.radiation sensitivity: An increased vulnerability to ionizing radiation because ATM-related DNA repair is impaired.

topics.heading: A-T research
topics.description: Research into ATM biology, DNA repair, neurodegeneration, immune function, infection, cancer risk, lung disease, biomarkers and supportive care.

termDefinitions.DNA repair: Cellular processes that detect and correct damage in genetic material.
termDefinitions.ATM protein: A protein made from the ATM gene that helps coordinate responses to DNA damage and supports cell stability.
termDefinitions.A-T biomarker: A measurable feature studied to understand A-T, its complications or response to an intervention.
termDefinitions.ataxia outcomes: Measures describing coordination, function, health, wellbeing or other results in people with ataxia.

topics.heading: Genetics and diagnosis
topics.description: ATM inheritance, carrier status, genetic testing, neurological assessment, immune evaluation and tests used to understand A-T and its complications.

termDefinitions.ATM gene: A gene that provides instructions for a protein involved in DNA-damage responses; variants in both copies can cause A-T.
termDefinitions.ATM variant: A change in the ATM gene; its meaning depends on laboratory interpretation and clinical context.
termDefinitions.autosomal recessive: An inheritance pattern in which disease usually requires relevant variants in both copies of a gene.
termDefinitions.carrier: A person who has one disease-associated recessive variant and usually does not have the recessive condition itself.
termDefinitions.genetic testing: Laboratory analysis of DNA or related material to look for genetic variants; results require appropriate interpretation.
termDefinitions.alpha-fetoprotein: A blood protein that is often elevated in A-T and may support clinical assessment, but is not by itself diagnostic.
termDefinitions.immunoglobulin levels: Measurements of antibody proteins that help assess aspects of immune function.
termDefinitions.ataxia diagnosis: The clinical process of evaluating coordination problems, associated features and test results to determine their cause.

topics.heading: Living with A-T
topics.description: Daily life with A-T, including mobility, communication, school, work, respiratory health, fatigue, independence, safety and quality of life.

termDefinitions.living with ataxia-telangiectasia: Managing everyday life, health and wellbeing while living with A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T quality of life: The physical, emotional, social and practical effects of A-T and its care on daily life.
termDefinitions.A-T mobility: Movement, balance, transfers and access needs in the context of A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T communication: Speech, language and communication needs that may occur with A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T school support: Educational accommodations and coordinated support for a student with A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T self-management: Everyday strategies used with clinical care to track symptoms, support safety and coordinate appointments.

topics.heading: Caregiving and support
topics.description: Family caregiving, multidisciplinary coordination, education, communication, practical support and community resources for people affected by A-T.

termDefinitions.ataxia-telangiectasia caregiving: Practical, emotional and organizational support provided to a person living with A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T family support: Information and services intended to support families affected by A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T caregiver: A person who provides regular practical, personal or emotional support to someone with A-T.
termDefinitions.rare disease support: Services and resources for people and families affected by uncommon conditions.
termDefinitions.A-T community: People and organizations connected by A-T experience, support, advocacy or research.

topics.heading: Advocacy and awareness
topics.description: A-T advocacy, awareness, research funding, policy, access to specialist services and communication about the needs of affected families.

termDefinitions.ataxia-telangiectasia advocacy: Activities intended to improve awareness, services, research or policy for people affected by A-T.
termDefinitions.A-T awareness: Efforts to improve recognition and understanding of ataxia-telangiectasia.
termDefinitions.A-T research funding: Financial support for research into A-T biology, care, treatments or outcomes.
termDefinitions.rare disease policy: Rules or public initiatives affecting people with uncommon conditions and their access to care or research.
termDefinitions.ATM advocacy: Advocacy focused on ATM-related disease and the needs of affected people and families.
